correctness.rationale: The stationary characteristic-function formula is independently derived from the stated Poisson generator. The problem is exactly maximization of E[T_n(X)] at fixed E[X]; even n has an explicit zero-rate law. Odd n has an explicit global concave majorant, proved via negative Chebyshev second derivative and a C^1 flat splice. Jensen gives the universal upper bound, and explicit symmetric distributions attain it for all g including endpoints. The quadratic coefficient follows from exact curvature at the outermost Chebyshev maximum. The GHZ QFI follows from its exact two-dimensional off-diagonal evolution. Finite verifier checks corroborate the proof; they are not used to deduce universality.

originality.rationale: The exact Poisson characteristic-function decay law, generic lattice-kick exception and GHZ QFI are acknowledged prior facts. The asserted result is the all-size sharp inverse *minimum* of GHZ decay at fixed one-qubit decoherence and event rate, including parity and quadratic onset. Searches against the closest accessible primary full main text, related decoherence-free and moment-theory literature, indexed records, and published mathematical findings did not identify a broader theorem implying the complete envelope. Complete access to the expanded closest paper is a material residual risk, explicitly declared, not a negative coverage proof.
residual_risks: The expanded version of arXiv:2607.02962 and the original supplemental material (including a lattice-kick counterexample) were not read in full. It might already contain the complete calibrated parity minimization; if so originality would fail.
General classical moment-problem texts may hide an equivalent all-Chebyshev concave envelope under another terminology; no global novelty certification or exhaustive indexing is claimed.
The exact minimizing distributions use atoms; slight continuous jitter generally reintroduces decay, and no robustness guarantee is asserted.

value.rationale: Given the experimentally meaningful calibrations Γ and Γ_1, the result distinguishes possible perfect GHZ preservation from forced positive loss and proves a sharp n-parity barrier, a nontrivial local-noise threshold and exact onset curvature. This fills a natural inverse-calibration gap in recent finite-jump noisy metrology. It is not the routine evaluation of the known characteristic function at a preset law: it optimizes all probability measures and classifies the feasible boundary. Atomic-law physical idealization and absence of independent audit are declared.
